title: Compact Alert Cardlets + Handoff Clipboard — prototype & usability feedback
creator: Amina Patel
description: Purpose: Design a compact alert surface ("cardlets") that surfaces essential SLO/alert context in dashboards and incident views, paired with a "handoff clipboard" — a transient, shareable bundle containing incident links, runbook snippets, next steps, and postmortem anchors for fast on-call transfer. Goals: 1) Reduce cognitive load during shift handoffs by providing a one-click clipboard for context transfer; 2) Improve mean time to recovery (MTTR) by surfacing the 3 most relevant context items per alert (recent related errors, a short runbook excerpt, and last deploy); 3) Keep console real-estate dense so dashboards remain scannable at glance. Success metrics: decrease median handoff time by 20% (measured via telemetry on clipboard usage and time between assignee change events), increase adoption of postmortem linking in incidents by 30%, and no regression in accessibility score (WCAG AA) for the affected screens. Scope: prototype UI patterns for alert cardlets (compact, expanded, pinned) and the handoff clipboard (ephemeral tray + share link + copy-to-clipboard). Exclusions: deep integrations (Slack/Teams webhook delivery) deferred to ENG backlog item. Key components: - Alert cardlet header with microstatus (SLO breach / warning / info), short title, truncated context snippet (max 120 chars), and quick actions (Acknowledge, Snooze, Open clipboard). - Expansion overlay that shows 3 prioritized context rows: recent error sample, last deploy timestamp, and a 1-2 line runbook excerpt with a 'Show full runbook' link. - Handoff clipboard tray: collects selected cardlets/incident artifacts; allows adding free-text notes and selects recipients; persistent share link and ephemeral copy; attach postmortem anchor (checkbox). - Microinteractions: shelf animation for clipboard, toast confirmation on copy/share, keyboard shortcut (Shift+H) to open clipboard. Accessibility considerations: full keyboard focus order, meaningful ARIA labels for status chips, high-contrast colors for microstatus. Instrumentation hooks: event names suggested: console.alert.cardlet.opened, console.alert.cardlet.clipboard_added, console.handoff.clipboard_shared, console.alert.cardlet.acknowledged. Acceptance criteria: - Prototype validated in 6 moderated sessions with SRE/on-call engineers and achieve at least 80% task success for creating and sharing a handoff bundle. - Design spec ready for handoff to ENG with annotated Figma and a checklist of feature flags and telemetry. - Edge cases documented (large runbook excerpts, alerts with >50 related traces, missing runbook). Trade-offs and decisions: chose ephemeral clip + share link over full integrations to accelerate launch and measure usage; compact cardlet truncation capped at 120 chars to keep dashboards scannable but includes 'expand' affordance for deeper context. Next steps: finalize copy, incorporate UX research notes, iterate on microcopy for clipboard sharing prompts, and create a low-fi A/B test to measure whether 'add runbook excerpt' should be default visible or hidden behind expand.
comments: 2025-09-19 - Jonah Ruiz (Design review): Clean interaction model. Suggest switching the 'Acknowledge' quick action to a confirmation modal when SLO impact is high. Also request localized strings planning.
2025-09-22 - Priya Menon (PM): Love the clearinghouse concept. Please add a product metric to measure 'handoff-to-first-action' time. Flagging ENG dependency for clipboard share link generation.

2025-09-25 - Marco Li (Eng - Runtime): Reminder: we need to avoid heavy API calls when rendering dashboards. For the cardlet expansion, prefer pre-fetched 'small context' payload with lazy load for full runbook text. Adding ENG-7923 as dependency.

2025-09-27 - Eva Gomez (UX Research): Completed 6 moderated sessions (SREs, on-call devs). Key findings: participants used the clipboard for 78% of handoffs in tasks; confusion around 'pin vs add to clipboard' — we should rename 'pin' to 'keep in dashboard'. Also two participants wanted Slack export. See recordings.

2025-10-01 - Jonah Ruiz (Design update): Updated microcopy after research. Resolved 'pin' wording, added 'copy summary' affordance, and adjusted color token for degraded status per accessibility review. Preparing final prototype for internal design critique on 2025-10-03.

2025-10-02 - Derek Shaw (Security): Quick note — share links must be single-use or time-limited to prevent information leakage. Marking for security review in the next sprint if we decide persistent links are supported.
